newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan relaxes LPG stockpile requirements.
newsitem.headline: Japan relaxes LPG stockpile requirements.

text.p: Japan's Agency of Natural Resources and Energy said on Friday it has relaxed requirements on mandatory liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) stockpiles on the back of soaring international LPG prices.
A Japanese law requires LPG importers to maintain stockpiles equivalent to a minimum of 50 days of imports.

Although the required volume has not been changed, the government now allows importers to temporarily borrow LPG cargoes from other importers to meet the required volume, a senior official at the agency said.
The relaxed rule enables those importers whose stockpile levels are below the requirement to borrow cargoes from firms with enough stocks, until its import cargoes arrive.
The borrowing and lending are expected to happen on paper without physical movements, he said.
Japanese importers of LPG have been asking the government to relax the stockpile requirements in order to avoid setting a bullish tone in the spot market by buying spot cargoes.
The world's largest LPG supplier Saudi Aramco sets its LPG contract prices based on the company's own assessments of spot market trends as well as the results of three monthly tenders.
Saudi Arabia's contract prices have a massive impact on the international LPG market as term prices of most LPG cargoes originating east of Suez are linked to Aramco prices.
